slide.text: The procurement case is not only about digitization. It is about reducing friction in land administration, Certificate of Occupancy processing, approvals, and public revenue capture.

text.p: Across Nigeria, delays in land and approval workflows do not only slow service delivery. They weaken formalisation, reduce confidence in records, raise project costs, and make it harder for states to convert approvals into reliable internally generated revenue.

The most persistent bottlenecks sit at the boundaries between parcel context, agency review, field evidence, legal progression, and supervisory follow-through. When those boundaries remain manual or disconnected, Certificate of Occupancy pipelines, planning approvals, and extractives workflows become harder to govern and harder to trust.

p.strong: That is why this should be treated as procurement of delivery infrastructure, not merely procurement of software screens.

tr.td: Why it matters in procurement terms
Slow approvals directly affect housing supply, developer confidence, and the speed at which formal projects can reach market.[1]
Low formalisation constrains mortgage depth, land-market confidence, and the visibility of fee and registration value for states.[1]
Mining and energy approvals need transparent review, evidence continuity, and stronger supervisory traceability.[2]
Disconnected parcel, legal, field, and approval records create leakage, slower turnaround, and weaker defensibility of public decisions.

slide.text: A procurement-grade platform must therefore improve service speed, revenue assurance, land certainty, and institutional trust at the same time.
